recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any renewed requirement for Communication.sender and Communication.recipient to have exactly identical, alphabetized targetProfile lists should be raised as a new Patient Care decision because it would alter later applied tracker outcomes.
issue_request: FHIR-5850 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution asking to add Organization to Communication receiver and make the sender and receiver reference-resource lists identical and alphabetical.
initial_application: Historical git commit a47e7d33aa1bc0c16baec2397ef964e6f8975053, corresponding to SVN 4977, applied #5850 by changing Communication.sender and receiver/recipient to Reference(Device|Organization|Patient|Practitioner|RelatedPerson) and updating Communication narrative to include organizations.
additional_context: Communication is still an active build resource. Current StructureDefinition source includes Organization in both Communication.recipient and Communication.sender. Later decisions intentionally expanded and differentiated the lists: FHIR-8466 added Group as recipient, FHIR-12817 added CareTeam as recipient, FHIR-17448 added HealthcareService and recorded that Group/CareTeam sender/recipient differences were warranted, FHIR-22630 added Endpoint to both sides, FHIR-26619 added CareTeam to sender, and FHIR-40760 recognizes current recipient examples including Location.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source change was made because forcing current targetProfile lists to be identical or merely re-sorting them would either undo later decisions or create editorial churn without changing implementer understanding.
